label: F-a36c3c

findings.note: Plan D3 maps claude-opus-5-5/claude-sonnet-5-5/gpt-oss-120b to antigravity/3p on purpose and says why (the quota of a row configured against vendor-routing is still a fact); the table at AgyQuotaReport.cs:40 changes no routing.
AgyError.cs:80 SkipWhile with a Func over a few stderr characters only keeps methods within complexity 4; no doctrine forbids it, and it does not run in a hot path.
QuotaCooldowns.cs:144 writes valid ISO 8601 UTC with a Z (whole seconds have no fraction), which is what the plan's common.utc-timestamps asks for; the choice of format is taste.

The key is computed in two places (QuotaCooldownRound.cs:62 from Request.Environment, PanelService.cs:419 from _keys), but every runtime sets *_API_KEY exactly when settings.ApiKey (= _keys.Keys[KeyName], RosterBuilder.cs:531) is non-empty (ReviewerRuntime.cs:725, ClaudeRuntime.cs:116, AntigravityRuntime.cs:71), so the described mismatch does not occur today.
At AgyError.cs:121-126 the loop guard stops at at >= Length, and Math.Min clamps the result, so a trailing escape can never index out of bounds, as the finding itself admits.
ClosingQuote (AgyError.cs:118-127) clamps to text.Length, and Balanced's loop (:95) then gets at = Length+1, which fails at < Length, so there is no infinite loop and no IndexOutOfRangeException.

The reader side is wrong: AtomicFile moves a whole file in place, so ReadAllText (QuotaCooldowns.cs:272) never sees partial text, and the plan decides fail-open with a single warning. The real contention is on the writer side: a reader's open handle can make Windows refuse the move.
Balanced starts after the marker (AgyError.cs:74,92), not at a log preamble; an unmatched } gives a slice that fails JsonDocument.Parse and is dropped as no error, which is the intended behaviour.
Plan D4 says explicitly 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever)'; PanelService.cs:418-420 does exactly that.
This repeats index 5: the bound check at AgyError.cs:121 plus Math.Min stop any out-of-bounds access, and one substring per AGY_ERROR line is not a performance issue.
Left (PanelService.cs:442) is only called for an entry that Standing returned with UntilUtc > now; '1 min' for under a minute is the round-up the plan asks for (D9).
Plan D3 specifies `string QuotaKeyOf(string model)` and string keys in the file; a typed wrapper asks for something the plan did not decide.

Plan D1 decides `bool? Spent` with null meaning 'read the text as today'; the implementation (QuotaCooldownRound.cs:108) follows the spec, and the finding admits it is a conflict between documents, not a code defect.
aCoolingRowSaysWhenItIsBack.test.ts:87 passes `state as never` to catalogHtml, so the type checker does not see the fixture; this is minor, and the same pattern exists in other test files.

Created() (QuotaCooldowns.cs:181-193) catches IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException exactly as D4 says; a data dir with a null character would break the server long before this point, and AfterRoundAsync still logs it without throwing.
Plan §11 plan-gate F0 rejected a hard size cap on purpose (eviction could un-park a spent row); expired entries drop at every write (QuotaCooldowns.cs:205), and notes are capped (:243).

The foreach at QuotaCooldownRound.cs:69-75 does probe one key at a time, but only agy keys with a known group probe (AntigravityRuntime.cs:195), so the worst case is three keys × 30 s, not ten; the plan does not specify running probes in parallel.
This duplicates index 15; the plan rejected this bound explicitly (§11 F0) and gives the 16 KiB budget reasoning in §8.

missed: QuotaCooldowns.Written (QuotaCooldowns.cs:214) calls AtomicFile.Write with no sharingRetry. The file is read on every CanRun and on every 10 s panel probe by several coai-mcp processes, so on Windows a reader's handle can make the move fail once (AtomicFile.cs:36-41). The round's whole park/lift aggregate is then refused. Other polled stores (SessionStore, Escalations, ConsultHealth) pass AtomicFile.SharingRetry.
summary: Of 18 findings, one is fully real (a minor test cast) and three are partly real but overstated. Six ask for things the plan decided against (Claude models on the 3p row, bool? Spent, no cache, string keys, no size cap twice), and three describe an out-of-bounds or infinite-loop bug that the code at AgyError.cs:121-126 already prevents. A team would gain almost nothing from acting on this review, and it missed the real Windows write-contention gap in the cooldown store.
